snippet.title: The Most Critical 10 Minutes of the D-Day Invasion
snippet.description:
Check out the HABU watch, exclusively available at: https://www.recwatches.com/timepieces/habu/  

Buy a Poster! https://www.historigraph.media/store
Get Early Access to Videos: https://www.patreon.com/historigraph 

Shortly after midnight on June 6th 1944, a glider passes silently over the Normandy countryside before crash landing in a field close to the caen canal. On board are the very first Allied troops to arrive in France on D-Day.  Their mission is to seize a vital bridge before the Germans could blow it sky high—and then hold it at all costs. If they fail, the very fate of the invasion could hang in the balance: this is the story of Pegasus Bridge. 

0:00 - Introduction
0:41 - The Most Important Bridge in Normandy
4:25 -  The Plan and the Men to Carry it Out
8:10 - Tip of the Spear 
11:46 - The Battle for the Bridges 

Sources: 

Will Fowler, Pegasus Bridge: Benouville D-Day 1944
Neil Barber, Pegasus Bridge: The capture, defence and relief of the caen canal and river orne bridges on D Day
Stephen Ambrose, Pegasus Bridge 

Film: The Longest Day, 1962

Credits:

Artwork by: 

chrisbyflanker.bsky.social

Animation by Josh Bassett and CKD Productions

snippet.title: The Turkish War of Independence (1919-1922) Every Day
snippet.description:
After the Ottoman defeat in World War I, the Treaty of Sèvres carved up Anatolia between the Allied powers, Greece, Armenia, and France. But a nationalist movement under Mustafa Kemal Atatürk, organized around the Grand National Assembly in Ankara, refused to accept the partition.

Watch the front lines shift every single day across three theaters of war the Greek invasion in the west, the Armenian campaign in the east, and the French in Cilicia to the south. From the Greek landing at Smyrna to the decisive Battle of Sakarya and the Great Offensive at Dumlupınar, see how the borders of modern Turkey were forged in just three years, culminating in the Treaty of Lausanne.

snippet.title: The Six-Day War: Every Day on Map (1967) | Israel vs Arab Coalition REMAKE
snippet.description:
In June 1967, the Middle East was a powder keg. Surrounded by mobilized Arab armies and facing a crippling naval blockade, Israel stood at the brink of destruction. But instead of waiting, they struck first.

On the morning of June 5, roaring jets launched a devastating preemptive strike. Within hours, the air forces of Egypt, Syria, and Jordan were obliterated on the ground. The most lightning fast conflict in modern military history had begun.

War tore across three fierce fronts: the burning sands of the Sinai Peninsula, the ancient streets of Jerusalem and the West Bank, and the rugged Golan Heights. Unable to halt Israel's rapid armored blitz, the Arab coalition quickly collapsed.

When the guns fell silent on June 10, the world was stunned. The map of the Middle East was completely redrawn, with Israel's territory tripling in size. Yet, these six days didn't bring peace they planted the seeds for decades of bitter conflict that still shape the region today.

What exactly happened during those six blazing days? Let's look at the map!

snippet.title: Why didn't Germany stop expanding in 1939? (Short Animated Documentary)
snippet.description:
Before the outbreak of World War 2 in 1939, Germany had been expanding rapidly, gaining the territories of the Saarland, Austria, the Sudetenland and Memel as well as turning Czechoslovakia into two puppet states. In spite of all these gains, German leaders still pushed for the return of Danzig and some territories around it and led to the outbreak of World War 2. And given that Germany lost that and then lost a great deal more territory, why didn't the Germans stop expanding before starting a war? Why not just be happy with what they'd already gained? To find out watch this short and simple animated history documentary.

snippet.description: In November 1240, Batu Khan burned Kyiv to the ground. Under this Pax Mongolica, Prince Danylo of Galicia-Volhynia shrewdly submitted to the Mongols in 1246, using their suzerainty to shield his borderland realm from aggressive Catholic Kings in Poland and Hungary. #UkraineHistory #MongolEmpire #HistoryShorts #GaliciaVolhynia #KyivanRus #MedievalHistory #BatuKhan #easterneurope

In 1822, the future of a united Latin America hung in the balance, a crucial moment of untold history. Join us for a historical journey into historia latinoamericana, and discover the forces that pulled a continent apart.

snippet.title: Britain’s Worst Defeat of WWI - Russia's Great Winter Victory
snippet.description:
🎥 Watch 300+ exclusive videos on ✔ youtube ► https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCMmaBzfCCwZ2KqaBJjkj0fw/join and ✔ Patreon ► https://www.patreon.com/kingsandgenerals

Kings and Generals animated historical documentary series on modern warfare the Great War and the Ottoman history during the World War I. Previously we covered the Rise of the Ottoman Empire from the humble beginnings as a small Turkic Beylik to the Fall of Constantinople 1453 covering all the major battles including (https://youtu.be/TDLmsiqhgns) and the reign of Mehmet II (https://youtu.be/TbqMBfxtOTI). After the Ottoman victory at Gallipoli and Bulgaria’s entry into the First World War, Istanbul shifted troops across a vast empire to meet the challenges of 1916. In the frozen Caucasus, General Nikolai Yudenich launches a meticulously prepared Russian offensive against the supposedly impregnable fortress of Erzurum. Winter marches, surprise attacks, and brutal fighting for mountain forts shatter the Ottoman Third Army and send it reeling westward. But while the Ottomans lose Erzurum, they strike back elsewhere. In the Sinai desert, Kress von Kressenstein’s forces raid British outposts near Katia, exposing the vulnerability of the Suez Canal. Farther east, the siege of Kut becomes a catastrophe for the British Empire. Relief columns repeatedly smash against Ottoman trenches at Sheikh Sa’ad, the Wadi, Hanna, Dujaila, and Sannaiyat—suffering appalling losses as General Charles Townshend’s starving garrison waits in vain. This episode follows the Russian advance through Persia, the fall of Kut after 147 days, and the strategic consequences of Britain’s twin failures at Gallipoli and Mesopotamia. It is a story of snowbound assaults, desert raids, and one of the most devastating surrenders of the Great War. Across three fronts, commanders gamble men, artillery, supply lines, and imperial prestige at terrible human cost.
